law: Swift packages are reusable components of Swift, Objective-C, Objective-C++, C, or C++ code that developers can use in their projects.
They bundle source files, binaries, and resources in a way that’s easy to use in your app’s project.
Each Swift package requires a file in the main directory of the package — referred to as the package manifest.
When you create a Swift package, you use the PackageDescription library in the package manifest to list dependencies, configure localized resources, and set other configuration options.
The package manifest also allows you to define executable products, as well as plugins that Swift Package Manager can use to build other products in the manifest.
